BACKGROUND: tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py holds six state-exact regression fixtures for a design review (Finding 1 name guards, 2 recovery, 3 reveal matching). Three are too weak. Read the file, tests/test_narration_corpus.py (house style, _late_scene_state builds a state with earlier scenes' entry facts and earned knowledge), tests/test_narration_term_traps.py, tests/test_leak_terms.py, tests/test_knowledge_leakage_matrix.py, and storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py plus storygame/story_package/loader.py (_compile_knowledge_indexes) to see which guard kinds exist. Keep the other three tests (missed_pointer, matcher_tie, more_than_four_eligible) unchanged.

TIGHTEN THESE THREE (keep the test function names ending in ordinary_name_accepted, premature_secret_rejected, skipped_reveal so the check finds them; you may add helper functions and extra tests, e.g. test_premature_secret_rejected_leak_term):
 1. ordinary_name_accepted: today it only asserts the turn does not raise. Make it a PAIRED test in one fixed early scene state: narration using an ordinary public scene name is accepted AND is actually committed (assert the accepted narration text appears in the engine's result or the state's recorded narration/log; find the real attribute), while in the SAME state narration with a protected term is rejected. Add a second ordinary-name case in a different scene so one scene's declarations are not the only evidence. Choose names that are really declared in the package (look them up, do not guess), and say in a comment why each is public.
 2. premature_secret_rejected: today both secret tests use the term JANUS. Cover at least THREE distinct guard kinds across at least two scenes, each asserted by exact error.code: (a) a protected term from a knowledge item's own protected/withheld terms, (b) a term declared through leak_terms, (c) an entity name (place/NPC/item) whose owners are not yet nameable (the entity-name scan in narration_safety.py). Parametrise with pytest.mark.parametrize and descriptive ids. If a kind has no usable real example, say so in notes.md and cover the others. Each case must first assert, with the real eligibility/knowledge helpers or by checking state facts, that the term's reveal is NOT yet earned in the state under test.
 3. skipped_reveal: model a real mid-game skip. Build a state in a LATER scene (for example 2C or 3A) the way _late_scene_state does (assert scene-entry facts for every earlier scene and the earned knowledge for earlier scenes) but deliberately leave ONE earlier reveal unearned: pick a reveal from an earlier scene whose text carries a protected term, and do not assert its establishes facts. Assert (i) the fact is absent in state, (ii) narration using that reveal's protected term is rejected with the exact error.code, and (iii) a control in the same state: the same term IS accepted when its reveal's establishes facts are asserted (copy the state, assert them, rerun). If current behaviour differs from (ii), assert the CURRENT behaviour and add a comment 'CURRENT DEFECT (review Finding 1): ...' explaining.
Rules: hermetic (no network, no env vars), whole file under 15 s, no xfail, player input strings are imperative commands in the player's voice ('Search the drawer.'), no 'Wait.'. Docstrings keep naming the review finding. Match the file's existing style; ruff-clean.

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py. Ruff: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix . and -m ruff format . . Reply with the files changed.
